attempted_claim: Let C be the 5-dimensional Cartan group with a fixed left-invariant rank-2 distribution, Carnot-Caratheodory metric, and homogeneous dimension Q=10, and use the analytic definition of K-quasiregularity (horizontal W^{1,Q}_{loc} regularity plus |D_H f|^Q <= K J_f a.e.). Fix distortion K=2 and omitting number 3. Decide: is every nonconstant 2-quasiregular self-map f:C->C omitting at least 3 distinct points necessarily constant? A complete answer is either a proof of constancy for this fixed K and this fixed omitting number with all capacity/Harnack steps verified, or one explicit nonconstant 2-quasiregular f:C->C with Sobolev regularity, distortion bound, and 3 distinct omitted values all rigorously verified.
decisive_failure: Both horns of the fixed-parameter dichotomy were blocked by verified quantitative gaps: generic capacity bounds overshoot omitting number 3 by orders of magnitude, and graded branching amplification prices minimal winding at K>=32 versus the allowed K=2; no alternative or emergent increment survived Audit scrutiny.
